Title: Comment on FR Doc # 2026-16965
Comment: This is not a renewable resource in the time we have. We need to protect these National treasures the way they are. Why are we moving backward on the progress we have made to restore these natural spaces? The environmental impact is irreversible, the impact on the people living near us irreversible. We will have no more wild spaces left for us to breathe explore research and learn from. This is illegal and should be in state control at least.

Title: Comment on FR Doc # 2026-16965
Comment: The current policies are sufficient and no change is needed.  Removing the roadless rule effectively strips our public lands of protections and resources that cannot be reversed.  It robs future generations of these public lands without the benefit of a return on investment. Any changes to the roadless rule need to be rejected.  Our public lands are for the public, not private benefit.  This proposal does not net the American public a benefit worthy of the cost, the sacrifice of these wilderness areas.  We need to keep the current roadless rule.

Title: Comment on FR Doc # 2026-16965
Comment: I think rescinding the roadless rule is very short-sighted.  Once the forests are destroyed we cannot bring them back, not to mention the harm putting roads in will do to our water and food supplies.   We're already seeing harm from clear cutting to build houses, stores, and data centers.  We are rapidly approaching the point of no return for the environment.   Please do not go forward with this.  Only a few greedy corporations actually want it.  Canvas actual real people not oligarchs, you'll see we want to keep the forests intact.

Title: Comment on FR Doc # 2026-16965
Comment: Keep these wildlife and natural areas protected. Keep this rule.

Title: Comment on FR Doc # 2026-16965
Comment: This has to be the most regressive rollback I’ve ever seen in my 26 years in this great country. Letting soft handed people decide what best for our protected forests is pathetic. These people who at most may have completed a 1 mile hike next to a populated roadway once in their life, don’t deserve to make these decisions and the person who wrote this bill should be tried for treason.

Title: Comment on FR Doc # 2026-16965
Comment: I am not in favor of changing this rule. Our national forests should be preserved. Please maintain the restrictions on road building in these areas

Title: Comment on FR Doc # 2026-16965
Comment: Do not change the current roadless areas policy. It will cause more problems & will cost more money that will not be good use of our tax dollars.

Title: Comment on FR Doc # 2026-16965
Comment: To give away the national treasure of these forests to private industry would be a great travesty for our country. To some it may seem like protecting these wild areas is a waste of resources but in a time of increasing technological advancements and the accompanying stress they impose these forests provide a much needed refuge from modern day life. They are an invaluable resource that need continued protection from the encroachment of out of control economic expansion at the expense of public welfare. This is not what our country was built on and is not good for the people.

Title: Comment on FR Doc # 2026-16965
Comment: I am commenting to let you know that i strongly oppose rescinding the 2001 roadless rule. After reading the proposal it is evident that they only want the rule revised so they can log all the timber. It is not worth it. Our National Forests are worth far more kept in tact. This is public land and should not be put up for sale to the highest bidding timber company

Title: Comment on FR Doc # 2026-16965
Comment: Keep the roadless rule.  Our national forests are a treasure.

Title: Comment on FR Doc # 2026-16965
Comment: This decision to rescind the roadless rule makes no sense if you are actually concerned about wildfire reduction and forest management.  Those things can be done under the current rules.  This feels like something else. Like you are interested in opening up these areas to different land use  and possible exploration and extraction of resources.  This is a good rule protecting millions of acres of habitat and backcountry.  Two things that actually do make this country great.  Rescinding the rule puts the benefits of this public land at risk, for the financial profit of a few.  Please don’t rescind the roadless rule.

Title: Comment on FR Doc # 2026-16965
Comment: Our public land needs to be protected. The roadless rule is here for a reason: conserving wildlife habitats, protecting watersheds, protecting drinking water, and supporting backcountry recreation. More roads, pavement and construction increase wildfire ignitions and threaten ecosystems. We don’t want our beautiful land turned into a hot pavement landscape. Protect nature. Value nature. Nature > corporate profits.

Title: Comment on FR Doc # 2026-16965
Comment: This is a horrible idea.  The roadless has been a success story for conservation.

Title: Comment on FR Doc # 2026-16965
Comment:
Please do not override the wishes of the public. 

Those lands belong to the PEOPLE of the United States. Do not repeal the Roadless Rule. 
All outdoorsmen want to see our public lands stay in tact for future generations. Opening them up to further destruction driven by the greed of the current administration and corporations is wrong. 

So many of you sitting in office have likely never even stepped foot on public lands to hunt, fish and recreate. Your idea of going outside is golfing - and golf courses destroy ecosystems and steal water, something we already don’t have enough of. 
Please see the photos of the land you are seeking to destroy by allowing reckless resource destruction. You may not care about these places, but WE DO. You do not own them. 

STOP THE REPEAL OF THE ROADLESS RULE. We, the people, demand you keep your hands off public lands. 

Stop the destruction of our remaining public owned National forests, BLM land, National Parks now!!

Title: Comment on FR Doc # 2026-16965
Comment: Please do not rescind the Roadless Rule.  This rule ensures that Wilderness Areas remain free of the negative effects of human impact.  I have enjoyed fishing, canoeing, and camping in these areas and know and appreciate how precious they are.
